title: Why start here?
text:
The planner can build a tour from several different starting points, and the choice decides which questions come next.

- **A club** – you already have a story club night in mind and want the nights around it filled in.
- **A venue** – you want to play a particular place and see what else is nearby.
- **A period** – you know when you are free (and roughly where) but not yet which gigs.
- **A venue pool** – you want a tour built from the kinds of venues other artists have played.

title: Why set a start and end?
text:
Travel is the real cost of a tour, so the planner needs to know where you are leaving from.

- The **start** is used to measure the first leg and to keep the search local.
- Tick **Finish back at the start** for a round trip, or give a different **end** if you are not going home.

Nothing is stored on a server: your start point stays in your own browser.

The distance limits from your start (and, in pool mode, to the first and from the last gig) sit in this panel, next to the start itself.

title: Why set a start and end?
text:
Travel is the real cost of a tour, so the planner needs to know where you are leaving from and where you need to end up.

- The **start** and **end** are used to cost the journey to the first gig and home again.
- Use the **first gig** and **last gig** limits if you have to get there after work, or must get home after the last show.

Nothing is stored on a server: your start point stays in your own browser.

The distance limits from your start (and, in pool mode, to the first and from the last gig) sit in this panel, next to the start itself.

title: Why pick an anchor gig?
text:
An anchor is the one gig you are sure about. The planner builds outwards from it, looking at the days before and after for other gigs within reach.

Pick the **month** first to narrow the list of dates, then the **anchor gig / date**.

title: Why choose artists?
text:
Touring is easier when you copy what already works. If you are a similar size to other artists, the venues they have played are venues that book acts like you.

- Add one or more **artists** or **tours**; the first artist you add is the **primary** one.
- The ★ on a chip makes someone else the primary.
- Or pool by **type of act** (all storytellers, musicians or poets).

The weekday rule keeps a venue to the days of the week these artists actually played it.

title: Why preview the pool?
text:
Before building a route, check that the pool looks right.

- Cards show each venue, who played it and on which weekdays.
- **New to you** marks venues none of your chosen artists has played, but a similar artist has.
- Untick venues you do not want, or click the dots on the map.

The lens controls (shared, only mine, played by all…) are for spotting overlap and gaps between artists.

title: Why set dates and weekdays?
text:
The planner can only offer gigs that fall inside your window, so keep it as tight as you realistically can (at most 21 days).

In pool mode, **Gigs wanted** is how many dates you want the route to contain.

**Only use a venue on a day of the week these artists have played it** keeps the suggestions realistic: if an artist has only ever played a venue on Fridays, only Fridays are offered there. Untick it to try any weekday.

In pool mode, once you have built options, the dates, area, must-visits and start/end move into panels beside the map and apply straight away, so you can tighten the tour while watching the options change. The weekday rule is also in the Filters panel.

title: Why limit the area?
text:
An area keeps a long period search from wandering across the whole country.

It defaults to your start point; give a different **centre** if you want to tour somewhere else, and a **radius** in road miles.

title: Why must-visits?
text:
Sometimes a tour has fixed points: a friend's gig, a venue that has invited you, a festival.

Add a **venue** or a **town**, set the date and how flexible you are (**exactly** or **± a few days**). The route is built so every must-visit is included.

Each place has a **status** that says how firm it is:
- **★ wish** – somewhere you'd like to play, on a day within the flexibility you set.
- **? queried** – you've asked the venue and have up to three possible dates; the planner uses exactly one of them, whichever suits the route best.
- **✎ pencilled** – a date is being held but isn't confirmed. It starts on your tour, but you can click it to release it if the venue says no (it stays released when you change filters, and returns when you press Develop tour again).
- **✓ booked** – confirmed: locked to that date, the only option that day, and exported as booked.

For pencilled and booked venues you can enter a number of **nights**. A run of consecutive nights counts as one visit to the venue, with no travelling between nights, though each night counts as a gig.

title: Why choose kinds of event?
text:
By default the planner uses story club nights and their specials.

Tick other kinds to use venues and gigs from:

- one-off story events
- music events
- poetry events
- folk nights
- Irish sessions

In "a venue" mode the same choice decides which venues appear in the list, so you can build around a music or poetry venue as easily as a story club.

In club and period modes, changing the kinds updates the options straight away. In venue mode this step comes first, because it decides which venues you can choose.

title: What happens when I build?
text:
**Develop tour** finds every gig that fits what you have set up and lays them out day by day, with the map beside them.

The required steps fold away afterwards (with a summary line you can expand). The panels beside the map, and the Filters, apply straight away, so you can keep adjusting while you look at the map and the day columns. Your picks are kept where they still fit.

**Save plan** downloads a small file with your set-up, picks and must-visits; **Load plan** puts it all back, so you can build a tour over several sittings.

title: Why these filters?
text:
These limits shape which routes are sensible, and they apply straight away.

- **Keep stops apart** avoids playing to the same audience twice.
- **Max miles between stops** keeps each hop drivable.
- **Max miles from start** keeps the whole tour local.
- **Visit each venue only once** stops the route returning to the same place.

title: Why these filters?
text:
These limits shape which gigs are sensible around your anchor, and they apply straight away.

- **When** sets how many days either side of the anchor to look at.
- **Where** limits how far apart gigs can be, and how far from your start.
- **Don't revisit** hides places too close to ones you have already chosen.

title: Why watch for clashes?
text:
Turn this on to see, on each option, whether something else is on that could split the audience:

- **red** – another event at the same venue that night
- **amber** – another event in the same town that night
- **grey** – an event in the same town the night before or after

Click a badge to see which events. It only warns: nothing is hidden or blocked.

Choose which kinds of event count. By default they match the kinds you're touring, so a music tour watches for music and a story tour for story. The artists you're touring are never counted as competition for themselves.

Only events listed in the directory are known, so no badge doesn't prove nothing else is on.
